news.title: 'Moreno System Also Captain SON' Son Heung-min: "World Cup was too painful... I will forget it and move forward"
news.lede: Son Heung-min (LAFC), captain of the South Korean national football team, declared his firm resolve to pour everything onto the field in order to win back fans' hearts ahead of the friendly match against Ecuador. On the 23rd, Son Heung-min attended the national team's official press conference at the Cheonan Football Center in Chungcheongnam-do alongside newly appointed coach Roberto Moreno. The team is set to face Ecuador on the 24th at 8 p.m. at Suwon World Cup Stadium for its first A-match of the month. news.title: Toni slams Juventus and Inter as he backs Mancini: ‘It is year zero for Italy’
news.lede: Luca Toni started every game of Italy’s 2006 World Cup win, from the opener against Ghana in Hanover to the final in Berlin, scoring twice against Ukraine in the quarter-finals along the way. Twenty years on, he has given a blunt assessment of a national team starting from nothing. Speaking to Tuttosport, the former striker did not soften it. “It is year zero by necessity, unless we start digging, in the sense that it cannot get worse after three failures to qualify for a World Cup,” Toni said.

news.title: Nigerian football experiencing ‘worst time in history’, says Afcon winner Segun Odegbami
news.lede: Nigeria's men failed to qualify for both the 2022 and 2026 Fifa World Cups. As Nigeria begin their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifying campaign, former international Segun Odegbami, who won the tournament on home soil in 1980, says the country is experiencing the "worst time" in its football history. Over the past 12 months both the Super Eagles and Super Falcons failed to qualify for their respective Fifa World Cups. But beyond the failure of the senior national teams, Nigeria has also endured disappointing results at age-group level and in African club competitions - although the West Africans recently reached the quarter-finals of the Under-20 Women's World Cup.

news.title: Scots recall Kerr & Thomas for World Cup play-offs
news.lede: Martha Thomas (left) and Sam Kerr (right) return to the Scotland squad for the first time since October. Sam Kerr and Martha Thomas have been named in their first Scotland squad in almost a year, as the experienced duo return for next month's Women's World Cup round one two-legged play-off against the Czech Republic. Melissa Andreatta's side travel to Pardubice, east of Prague, on Friday, 9 October before welcoming the Czechs to St Mirren Park four days later, eyeing progression to another two-legged play-off against either Sweden or Lithuania with a place at next summer's tournament in Brazil at stake.

news.title: UEFA boss Ceferin says trust in world football remains broken after FIFA investment row
news.lede: UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin said that said unity, transparency and governance that served the wider game were essential to maintaining trust in football. OEIRAS – UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin said trust in world football had not been restored following the collapse of FIFA’s controversial private-investment plan, in his first public comments since FIFA president Gianni Infantino offered a review of the governing body’s decision-making. In a video address to the Portugal Football Summit on Sept 23, Ceferin said unity, transparency and governance that served the wider game were essential to maintaining trust in football. “Yet not everyone places the game above their own ambitions,” Ceferin said.

news.title: Girls Football Festival brings friendship and opportunity to Montenegro
news.lede: Wednesday, September 23, 2026 by Aleksandar Radovic. The Girls Football Festival came to Montenegro for the first time this month, bringing together 80 girls from the region for three days of football, education and social activities. Founded in Vienna, the festival took place in the Austrian capital for six years before moving to Sarajevo in 2025. This year, it is continuing its mission of using football to promote friendship, inclusion and personal development, this time among young female players from Montenegro, Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

news.title: Cerebral Palsy Football World Cup to be Hosted in Fayette
news.lede: Soccer Federation is preparing to host the 2026 International Federation of Cerebral Palsy Football Men's and Women's World Cup, marking the first time in 20 years the tournament has been held in the United States. The tournament is scheduled Oct. 12-24 and will take place at Arthur M. Soccer National Training Centre. There will be 12 men's teams and eight women's teams, from six continents, competing this year, according to officials.
